reading.body:
Peking University holds 412 granted US patents, and its most recent grants are in memory arrays, deposition equipment, and medical materials, not AI models.

The patent record is the only substantive technical signal here. The five most recent grants, dated September 2026, cover a three-dimensional memory array, a vertical photo-assisted MOCVD apparatus, a medical material, an SVM training method, and an immunophenotyping reagent composition. Four of the five are hardware, materials, or biotech. One, the SVM training method, is machine learning, but it is a classical method rather than anything tied to large-scale model training.

For AI specifically, the relevant thread is memory. Three-dimensional memory arrays are the substrate that high-bandwidth memory is built on, and high-bandwidth memory is one of the components that constrains how fast accelerators can be fed. A university patenting in this area is a signal about where semiconductor research capacity sits, not a signal about AI compute being built. The MOCVD apparatus points the same direction, toward the deposition tools that make memory and logic possible.

What the data does not show is any AI product, any lawsuit, any MCP server, or any research program. The profile text describes campus services, bookstores, banking, and mail delivery, and states plainly that no AI products are identified. The patent count is a single aggregate from one source, USPTO grants since 2001 matching the applicant phrase "peking university," and it does not separate AI-related filings from the rest. Nothing here establishes a link between this institution and AI compute capacity, and the reader should not infer one.

profile_text.body:
Peking University is a university in Beijing, China, and its English-language site describes campus life and services rather than research or teaching programs. The site notes that being part of the university means access to a wide range of retail stores and services on campus, and it points visitors to information on campus services such as bookstores, banking, and mail delivery. The page carries a copyright notice for Peking University, an address at No.5 Yiheyuan Road, Haidian District, Beijing 100871, P.R.China, and Chinese filing numbers 京ICP备05065075号-1 and 京公网安备110402430047号.

The university is also known as PKU. It is a nonprofit institution, and the material available does not identify any AI products, lawsuits, or MCP servers associated with it.
